question: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 543.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Article 81 of the Constitution, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) has a maximum strength of 543 elected members representing territorial constituencies across the states and Union Territories. (लोकसभा — 543 सीटें)

 

• Additionally, up to 2 members of the Anglo-Indian community could earlier be nominated by the President, but this provision lapsed in January 2020 via the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act.

 

• The current total effective strength of the Lok Sabha (elected members) is 543, out of which 131 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes (84) and Scheduled Tribes (47).

 

• Seats are distributed among states roughly in proportion to population, based on the 1971 Census (frozen until the first census after 2026, as per the 42nd and 84th Amendments).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States), the upper house, has a maximum strength of 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated), with a current effective strength of 245.

 

• The tenure of the Lok Sabha is 5 years unless dissolved earlier, while the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with one-third of members retiring every two years.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (553, 523, 533): These are close but incorrect numbers; the constitutionally fixed maximum elected strength of the Lok Sabha is exactly 543.

question: In 1887, the Royal Society, London gave the Davy Medal for the ‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ to ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is John Alexander Newland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• John Alexander Reina Newlands, an English chemist, was awarded the Davy Medal by the Royal Society, London, in 1887 in recognition of his early contribution to the discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements. (डेवी पदक 1887 — जॉन अलेक्जेंडर न्यूलैंड्स)

 

• Newlands had earlier (1865) proposed the "Law of Octaves", arranging known elements in order of increasing atomic weight and observing that every eighth element had similar properties — an early precursor to the modern periodic law.

 

• Although his work was initially ridiculed by the scientific community, the Royal Society later recognised his priority and honoured him with the Davy Medal in 1887, five years after Mendeleev and Meyer received the same medal.

 

• The Davy Medal is an annual award of the Royal Society for an outstandingly important recent discovery in chemistry, instituted in 1877 in memory of Sir Humphry Davy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev and Lothar Meyer jointly received the Davy Medal in 1882 for their independent discovery of the periodic relations of atomic weights among the elements — a different, earlier award from the 1887 one referred to in this question.

 

• Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869) arranged elements by increasing atomic weight and left gaps for undiscovered elements, correctly predicting their properties.

 

NOTE

 

• AEB de Chancourtois (Option 1): A French geologist who proposed the "Telluric Screw" (Vis Tellurique) arrangement of elements in 1862, an early but largely overlooked periodic classification; he did not receive the 1887 Davy Medal.

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev (Option 2): Received the Davy Medal jointly with Lothar Meyer, but in 1882, not 1887.

 

• Lothar Meyer (Option 3): Also received the Davy Medal jointly with Mendeleev in 1882, not 1887.

question: Name the committee formed for the Village and Small-scale Industries in 1955?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karve Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Village and Small-Scale Industries (Karve) Committee was constituted in 1955 during the Second Five Year Plan period, chaired by Dr. D.G. Karve. (कर्वे समिति — ग्राम एवं लघु उद्योग, 1955)

 

• The committee recommended a decentralised, labour-intensive approach to industrialisation, promoting village and small-scale industries alongside large-scale industry to generate employment and utilise local resources.

 

• On the basis of its recommendations, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) was established in 1956–57 to promote and organise khadi and village industries across India.

 

• Other members of the committee included D.R. Gadgil, Vaikunth L. Mehta, P. Govindan Nair and V. Nanjappa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Second Five Year Plan (1956–61), guided by the Mahalanobis model, emphasised rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy and basic industries, alongside supporting small-scale sectors as recommended by the Karve Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• Rangarajan Committee (Option 1): Various committees under this name dealt with subjects like financial inclusion and poverty estimation, headed by economist C. Rangarajan, not village/small-scale industries in 1955.

 

• Basel Committee (Option 2): The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is an international body (established 1974) that sets global banking regulatory standards; unrelated to Indian village industries.

 

• Narasimhan Committee (Option 4): Headed by M. Narasimham, this committee (1991 and 1998) dealt with banking sector reforms in India, not village and small-scale industries.

question: In November 2022, technology Transfer Scheme is implemented by which of these states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In November 2022, the Kerala government launched the Technology Transfer Scheme, implemented through the Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment (KSCSTE). (प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण योजना — केरल)

 

• Under the scheme, the state government reimburses up to ₹10 lakh of the technology licensing cost to startups and MSMEs that acquire patented or proven technologies developed by KSCSTE-affiliated research institutions, to help them scale up commercially.

 

• The scheme aims to bridge the gap between research and industry, encouraging faster commercialisation of indigenous technologies developed within the state's research ecosystem.

 

• It is administered as part of Kerala's broader push to strengthen its innovation and startup ecosystem, complementing bodies like Kerala Startup Mission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• KSCSTE (Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment) is the nodal agency of the Kerala government for promoting scientific research, technology development and environmental protection in the state.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1), Andhra Pradesh (Option 2) and Maharashtra (Option 3): None of these states launched the Technology Transfer Scheme in November 2022; the scheme is specific to Kerala.

question: Who among the following performed a ritual called ‘hiranya-garbha’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dantidurga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dantidurga, the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, overthrew his Chalukya overlord (Kirtivarman II of Badami) in the mid-8th century CE and performed the Hiranya-garbha ("golden womb") ritual to legitimise his newly acquired sovereign status. (हिरण्यगर्भ अनुष्ठान — दंतिदुर्ग, राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• The Hiranya-garbha was a grand Vedic ritual traditionally performed by rulers to claim elevated, quasi-divine status and to be symbolically "reborn" as a Kshatriya of high rank, often used by rulers of non-traditional lineage to assert legitimacy.

 

• Dantidurga established the Rashtrakuta kingdom with its capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed), laying the foundation for later powerful rulers of the dynasty.

 

• His performance of this ritual is recorded in Rashtrakuta inscriptions and is cited by historians as an example of ritual legitimation of political power in early medieval India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dantidurga was succeeded by his uncle Krishna I, who is credited with commissioning the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.

 

• The Rashtrakutas ruled over large parts of the Deccan from the 8th to 10th centuries CE and were noted patrons of art, literature and architecture.

 

NOTE

 

• Govinda I (Option 2): An early, relatively obscure Rashtrakuta ruler; not associated with the hiranya-garbha ritual.

 

• Dhruva Dharavarsha (Option 3): A later, militarily prominent Rashtrakuta king known for the tripartite struggle for Kannauj; not linked with this ritual.

 

• Krishna I (Option 4): Successor of Dantidurga, remembered chiefly for the Kailasa Temple at Ellora, not for performing hiranya-garbha.

question: Which of the following Acts of the British Parliament stated that a member of the British Cabinet was appointed Secretary of State for India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act of 1858.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the Revolt of 1857, transferred the government of India from the East India Company directly to the British Crown. (भारत शासन अधिनियम 1858 — भारत सचिव का पद)

 

• It created the post of Secretary of State for India, a member of the British Cabinet, who was made responsible to the British Parliament for the governance of India and was assisted by a 15-member Council of India.

 

• The Act abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors of the East India Company, ending Company rule in India.

 

• The Governor-General of India was given the additional title of Viceroy, as the direct representative of the Crown; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy under this Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 later replaced the India Council with an advisory body and laid the framework for provincial autonomy.

 

• The Secretary of State for India post continued until Indian independence in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Council Act of 1861 (Option 1): Restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras presidencies and introduced Indians into the legislative process for the first time; did not create the Secretary of State post.

 

• Regulating Act, 1773 (Option 3): The first step by the British Parliament to control East India Company affairs in India; created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, long before the Crown took over.

 

• Charter Act of 1853 (Option 4): Separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council and introduced open competition for civil service recruitment; did not create the Secretary of State post.

question: Against whom was the Battle of Plassey (1751) fought by the English Company led by Robert Clive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siraj Ud Daulah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Plassey was fought between the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, on the banks of the Bhagirathi river near Plassey (Palashi) in Bengal. (प्लासी का युद्ध — सिराज उद-दौला)

 

• Siraj-ud-Daulah's defeat was largely engineered through the treachery of his own commander-in-chief, Mir Jafar, who had secretly conspired with the British in exchange for being installed as the new Nawab.

 

• The battle marked the beginning of British political control in India, as the English East India Company placed Mir Jafar on the throne of Bengal as a puppet Nawab after the victory.

 

• The victory gave the Company enormous wealth and access to Bengal's resources, setting the stage for the eventual establishment of British colonial rule across the subcontinent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764), fought against the combined forces of the Nawab of Bengal (Mir Qasim), Nawab of Awadh (Shuja-ud-Daulah) and Mughal Emperor (Shah Alam II), further consolidated British power and led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) and the grant of Diwani rights.

 

• Note: the Battle of Plassey was actually fought in 1757; the year "1751" in this question is a printing/typing slip in the source paper, but it does not affect the correct answer, which concerns the opposing ruler.

 

NOTE

 

• Nizam of Awadh (Option 1): Awadh had a Nawab, not a Nizam (the title "Nizam" is associated with Hyderabad); in any case, Awadh was not a party to the Battle of Plassey.

 

• Murshid Quli Khan (Option 3): An earlier Nawab of Bengal (early 18th century) who founded the line of independent Bengal Nawabs; he had died decades before the Battle of Plassey.

 

• Shaan Nawab (Option 4): Not a historical figure associated with the Battle of Plassey; a distractor option.

question: In July 2022, the Supreme Court accepted the report of the Banthia Commission. In its report, the commission recommended that OBCs should be given up to _______ reservation in local bodies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2022, the Supreme Court accepted the recommendations of the State Backward Classes Commission (Banthia Commission), headed by Jayant Kumar Banthia, in the context of OBC reservation in local body elections in Madhya Pradesh (following the SC's insistence on the "triple test"). (बांठिया आयोग — 27 प्रतिशत ओबीसी आरक्षण)

 

• The commission recommended that OBCs be given reservation of up to 27 percent in local bodies, subject to the overall cap that total reservation (SC + ST + OBC) should not exceed 50 percent of the seats in any local body.

 

• This reservation was to be applied following the "triple test" laid down by the Supreme Court: (i) setting up a dedicated commission to conduct rigorous empirical inquiry, (ii) specifying the proportion of reservation based on this inquiry, and (iii) ensuring the total reservation does not exceed 50%.

 

• Based on this report, the Supreme Court permitted the Madhya Pradesh State Election Commission to notify OBC reservation in the upcoming local body elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The "triple test" for local body OBC reservation was first laid down by the Supreme Court in Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v. State of Maharashtra (2021).

 

• Several other states (e.g., Gujarat) have similarly notified 27 percent OBC reservation in local bodies following empirical commission reports.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (15%, 24%, 20%): These figures do not match the Banthia Commission's actual recommendation of 27 percent OBC reservation.

question: The mode of transport to reach the most remote and distant areas which are most inaccessible is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Airways.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Airways are the fastest and most convenient mode of transport for reaching remote, distant and otherwise inaccessible areas, such as hilly, snow-bound, desert or forested regions where laying roads or railway lines is difficult or impossible. (वायु मार्ग — दुर्गम क्षेत्रों तक पहुंच)

 

• Air transport does not require a continuous physical track like roads or railways; it only needs terminal facilities (airports/airstrips/helipads) at the origin and destination, making it ideal for areas cut off by terrain.

 

• In India, air services (including helicopter services) connect otherwise inaccessible regions such as parts of the North-East, Ladakh, and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and are also vital during disaster relief operations.

 

• Though airways are the costliest mode of transport, their unmatched speed and ability to bypass difficult terrain make them indispensable for reaching the most remote locations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Waterways are the cheapest mode of transport for bulky goods over long distances but are restricted to navigable rivers, canals, and coasts.

 

• Railways are best suited for carrying heavy goods and passengers over long distances on land but require substantial fixed infrastructure.

 

NOTE

 

• Waterways (Option 1): Limited to areas with navigable water bodies; cannot reach landlocked, hilly or desert regions.

 

• Roadways (Option 2): Offer flexibility and door-to-door connectivity but are difficult and costly to construct in extremely rugged or inaccessible terrain.

 

• Railways (Option 3): Require heavy, level infrastructure and are the least adaptable to difficult or remote terrain among the options.

question: How many rights are mentioned under “Right to Equality”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Equality, guaranteed under Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution (Part III, Fundamental Rights), comprises five distinct rights. (समता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 14-18)

 

• Article 14: Equality before law and equal protection of laws.

 

• Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

 

• Article 16: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

 

• Article 17: Abolition of untouchability; and Article 18: Abolition of titles (except military and academic distinctions) — together these constitute the five rights under this head.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Right to Equality is enforceable against the State and, in certain respects (like Article 17 and 15(2)), against private individuals as well.

 

• Article 17 makes the practice of untouchability a punishable offence, further reinforced by the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (3, 6, 4): None of these match the actual count; Articles 14 through 18 give exactly five rights under the Right to Equality.

question: Which low-calorie sweetener has the chemical formula C14H18N2O5 that is two hundred times sweeter than sugar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aspartame.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aspartame has the chemical formula C₁₄H₁₈N₂O₅ and is a low-calorie artificial sweetener that is approximately 200 times sweeter than ordinary sucrose (table sugar). (एस्पार्टेम — चीनी से 200 गुना मीठा)

 

• Chemically, aspartame is a methyl ester of the dipeptide of the amino acids aspartic acid and phenylalanine.

 

• It is widely used in diet soft drinks, sugar-free chewing gums, and various low-calorie food products as a sugar substitute.

 

• Aspartame carries a warning label for people with phenylketonuria (PKU), a genetic disorder, since its metabolism releases phenylalanine.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saccharin (C₇H₅NO₃S) is about 300–400 times sweeter than sugar and was one of the earliest artificial sweeteners discovered (1879).

 

• Sucralose (C₁₂H₁₉Cl₃O₈) is derived from sucrose by chlorination and is about 600 times sweeter than sugar.

 

NOTE

 

• Saccharin (Option 1): Has a different formula (C₇H₅NO₃S) and a different sweetness multiple (~300-400x), not C₁₄H₁₈N₂O₅.

 

• Sucralose (Option 3): Chlorinated sugar derivative with formula C₁₂H₁₉Cl₃O₈, roughly 600 times sweeter than sugar — does not match the given formula.

 

• Neotame (Option 4): A derivative of aspartame with formula C₂₀H₃₀N₂O₅, about 7,000–13,000 times sweeter than sugar — does not match the given formula or sweetness value.

question: Techniques of making silk were first invented in China around _____ years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to widely cited historical and archaeological accounts, the techniques of sericulture (silk production) were first developed in China around 7000 years ago, making it one of the oldest known textile crafts. (रेशम निर्माण तकनीक — चीन, लगभग 7000 वर्ष पूर्व)

 

• Legend attributes the discovery of silk to Empress Leizu (Xi Ling Shi), wife of the mythical Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), who is said to have discovered silk when a cocoon fell into her cup of hot tea.

 

• Silk is obtained from the cocoons of the silkworm (Bombyx mori), which feeds on mulberry leaves; China guarded the secret of silk-making for centuries, giving rise to the famous Silk Road trade route.

 

• China remained the world's dominant silk producer for millennia before sericulture techniques eventually spread to other regions such as Korea, Japan, India and the Byzantine Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is the second-largest producer of silk in the world after China, and is the only country producing all five commercial varieties: Mulberry, Tasar, Eri, Muga and Oak Tasar silk.

 

• Karnataka is traditionally India's largest producer of mulberry silk.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (3000, 9000, 5000): These figures do not match the commonly cited estimate of ~7000 years for the origin of Chinese silk-making techniques.

question: The first edition of the Common wealth Youth Games was organised in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games was held in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 2000, organised for young athletes (typically aged 14-18) from Commonwealth nations. (राष्ट्रमंडल युवा खेल — पहला संस्करण, एडिनबर्ग 2000)

 

• The Commonwealth Youth Games are held once every four years, modelled on the senior Commonwealth Games, and act as a platform to nurture young sporting talent from member nations.

 

• Subsequent editions were held in Bendigo, Australia (2004), Pune, India (2008), Isle of Man (2011), Samoa (2015), and Bahamas (2017).

 

• India hosted the 3rd Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune in 2008.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) oversees both the senior Commonwealth Games and the Commonwealth Youth Games.

 

NOTE

 

• 2008 (Option 1): This was the year of the third Commonwealth Youth Games, held in Pune, India — not the first.

 

• 2012 (Option 2): No Commonwealth Youth Games edition was held in this specific year.

 

• 2016 (Option 4): No Commonwealth Youth Games edition was held in this specific year; the closest editions were 2015 (Samoa) and 2017 (Bahamas).

question: The ceremony that marks the end of Republic Day celebrations is ________.
option_2: the fly-past by the Indian Air Force fighter aircraft
option_3: the ‘At Home’ ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhawan
option_4: the homage ceremony at National War Memorial
solution_text:
The correct answer is the beating retreat ceremony.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Beating Retreat ceremony, held on the evening of 29 January every year at Vijay Chowk, New Delhi, officially marks the conclusion of the multi-day Republic Day celebrations. (बीटिंग रिट्रीट समारोह — गणतंत्र दिवस समापन)

 

• It features performances by the military bands of the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force, along with the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), and traditionally ends with the tune of "Sare Jahan Se Achha" and "Abide with Me" (Mahatma Gandhi's favourite hymn).

 

• The ceremony originates from an old military tradition where troops would cease fighting at sunset, sound the retreat, and withdraw from the battlefield, later evolving into a ceremonial ritual to lower and fold flags for the day.

 

• The President of India is the chief guest of the ceremony as the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Republic Day (26 January) commemorates the date the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950, and celebrations traditionally run from 26 to 29 January.

 

• The main Republic Day parade takes place at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), New Delhi, showcasing India's military strength and cultural diversity.

 

NOTE

 

• The fly-past by the Indian Air Force fighter aircraft (Option 2): This is part of the main Republic Day parade itself on 26 January, not the concluding ceremony.

 

• The ‘At Home’ ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhawan (Option 3): A separate reception hosted by the President on Republic Day; it does not mark the formal end of the celebrations.

 

• The homage ceremony at National War Memorial (Option 4): The Prime Minister pays homage to fallen soldiers on the morning of 26 January, before the parade begins — not the concluding event.

question: Which of the following pairs of countries hosted the FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poland and Slovenia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship was jointly hosted by Poland and Slovenia, held from 26 August to 11 September 2022. (एफआईवीबी पुरुष विश्व चैंपियनशिप 2022 — पोलैंड और स्लोवेनिया)

 

• The tournament was originally scheduled to be co-hosted by Russia, but the FIVB relocated the event to Poland and Slovenia following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which led to Russia's suspension from international volleyball competitions.

 

• The final was played at the Tauron Arena in Kraków, Poland.

 

• Italy won the tournament, defeating Poland 3-1 in the final to claim their fourth world title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship is organised by the Fédération Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB) and is held every four years.

 

• The previous edition, held in 2018, was co-hosted by Italy and Bulgaria, with Poland winning that title.

 

NOTE

 

• Bulgaria and Slovenia (Option 1): Not the actual host pair; Bulgaria co-hosted the 2018 edition (with Italy), not 2022.

 

• Italy and Bulgaria (Option 2): This pair hosted the 2018 edition, not 2022.

 

• Italy and Poland (Option 4): These were the two finalists of the 2022 tournament, not its hosts; the actual hosts were Poland and Slovenia.

question: Polar easterlies are which kind of winds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Permanent winds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Polar easterlies are permanent (planetary) winds that blow from the polar high-pressure belts (around 90° N/S) towards the sub-polar low-pressure belts (around 60° N/S), deflected westward by the Coriolis effect to blow from the north-east in the Northern Hemisphere and south-east in the Southern Hemisphere. (ध्रुवीय पूर्वी हवाएं — स्थायी पवनें)

 

• Permanent (planetary) winds blow consistently throughout the year over large areas in a fairly fixed direction, driven by the global pattern of pressure belts; the three main permanent wind systems are the Trade Winds, Westerlies, and Polar Easterlies.

 

• Polar easterlies are relatively cold, dry and dense winds, given the extremely low temperatures of the polar regions from which they originate.

 

• They play a role in driving polar climate patterns and interact with the westerlies at the sub-polar low-pressure belt, contributing to mid-latitude weather systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Seasonal winds (e.g., monsoons) change direction with the seasons; local winds (e.g., land and sea breeze, loo) blow over small areas due to local temperature/pressure differences.

 

• The other two permanent wind belts are the Trade Winds (from sub-tropical high to equatorial low) and the Westerlies (from sub-tropical high to sub-polar low).

 

NOTE

 

• Seasonal winds (Option 1): These reverse direction with seasons, e.g. monsoon winds; polar easterlies blow in a fixed direction year-round.

 

• Sea storm (Option 3): Refers to a stormy weather event at sea, not a category of prevailing global wind system.

 

• Local winds (Option 4): These operate over small, localized areas (e.g., land/sea breezes); polar easterlies are large-scale, planetary-level winds.

question: _______ took over the charge of Director General of Employees’ State Insurance Corporation in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajendra Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Rajendra Kumar, a senior IAS officer, took over as Director General of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) in October 2022. (कर्मचारी राज्य बीमा निगम — राजेंद्र कुमार, अक्टूबर 2022)

 

• The ESIC is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, providing socio-economic protection to workers in the organised sector and their dependents through medical, sickness, maternity, and disability benefits.

 

• The Director General is the apex executive head responsible for the administration of ESIC's schemes across India.

 

• ESIC was established under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• ESIC operates the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme, a self-financing social security and health insurance scheme for Indian workers earning below a specified wage ceiling.

 

NOTE

 

• Ravi Mittal (Option 1): Served as Secretary, Department of Sports, Government of India — a different post.

 

• Suchitra K Ella (Option 2): Co-founder of Bharat Biotech, a vaccine manufacturing company — unrelated to ESIC.

 

• Ajay Bhushan Pandey (Option 3): A former Finance Secretary and Revenue Secretary of India, and Chairman of the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) — not the ESIC Director General in October 2022.

question: Identify the longest part of bacterial flagellum.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Filament.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The bacterial flagellum is composed of three main structural parts: the basal body, the hook, and the filament, and among these, the filament is the longest part. (जीवाणु कशाभिका — तंतु (filament) सबसे लंबा भाग)

 

• The filament is a long, thin, whip-like helical structure made up of the protein flagellin, extending outward from the cell surface and functioning as the propeller that drives bacterial motility.

 

• The hook is a short, curved segment that connects the filament to the basal body and acts as a universal joint, transmitting torque from the motor to the filament.

 

• The basal body anchors the flagellum to the cell membrane/wall and contains the rotary motor (powered by proton motive force) that drives flagellar rotation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bacteria may be classified by flagellar arrangement as monotrichous (single flagellum), lophotrichous (tuft at one end), amphitrichous (one flagellum at each end), or peritrichous (flagella all over the surface).

 

• Flagellar rotation in bacteria can be clockwise or counter-clockwise, controlling whether the cell moves in a smooth "run" or randomly "tumbles", forming the basis of bacterial chemotaxis.

 

NOTE

 

• Basal body (Option 1): The anchoring, motor-containing base of the flagellum embedded in the cell envelope — not the longest part.

 

• Hook (Option 2): A short flexible connector between the basal body and filament — the shortest of the three named structures.

 

• Tail (Option 3): Not a standard term for a distinct part of the bacterial flagellum; the correct term for the long external whip-like structure is the filament.

question: Borgeet, a musical composition, is used in which of the following classical dances of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Borgeet (also spelt Borgit), a genre of lyrical devotional songs, is closely associated with the Sattriya dance form of Assam. (बरगीत — सत्रिया नृत्य, असम)

 

• Borgeets were composed primarily by the Vaishnavite saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev and his disciple Madhavdev in the 15th-16th centuries, forming an integral part of the Ekasarana Dharma (Neo-Vaishnavite) devotional tradition of Assam.

 

• Sattriya, one of the eight classical dance forms of India (officially recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000), originated in the Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) of Assam, founded by Sankardev.

 

• Sattriya dance-drama performances (known as Ankiya Naat) traditionally incorporate Borgeet as accompanying music for their devotional and narrative content.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dances of India are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 1): Associated with Ras Lila performances and devotional music of Manipur, not Borgeet.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A North Indian classical dance form rooted in storytelling traditions of temple and court, not linked to Borgeet.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 4): A Tamil Nadu classical dance form performed to Carnatic music, unrelated to Assam's Borgeet tradition.

question: Which of the following cells line the spongocoels and canals in members of the phylum Porifera?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Collar cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Collar cells, also known as choanocytes, line the spongocoel (central cavity) and the internal canal system of sponges (phylum Porifera). (कॉलर कोशिकाएं (चोआनोसाइट्स) — पोरीफेरा)

 

• Each choanocyte has a flagellum surrounded by a collar of microvilli; the beating of the flagella creates water currents that circulate water through the sponge's canal system, drawing in food particles and oxygen.

 

• Choanocytes are responsible for filter feeding — they trap suspended food particles from water using their collar and then engulf them via phagocytosis.

 

• Porifera (sponges) are simple, sessile, aquatic, multicellular animals exhibiting cellular level of organisation and characterised by a system of pores (ostia), canals, and the central spongocoel through which water flows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The body of a sponge is supported by a skeleton of spicules (calcareous or siliceous) or spongin fibres, which also aids in classification of sponges.

 

• Pinacocytes form the outer covering (pinacoderm) of sponges, distinct from the choanocytes lining the internal canals.

 

NOTE

 

• Somatic cells (Option 1): A general biological term for ordinary body cells (as opposed to reproductive cells), not a specific poriferan cell type lining canals.

 

• White cells (Option 3): Not a recognised cell type of the poriferan canal system; this term is generally associated with leukocytes in blood.

 

• Sex cells (Option 4): Refer to gametes (reproductive cells) of sponges, which are produced within the mesohyl, not cells lining the spongocoel/canals.

question: Chilika lake is situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chilika Lake, the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second-largest lagoon in the world, is situated in the state of Odisha, spread across the districts of Puri, Khordha and Ganjam. (चिल्का झील — ओडिशा)

 

• It is a brackish water lagoon, separated from the Bay of Bengal by a sandy ridge, and was designated as India's first Ramsar site (wetland of international importance) in 1981.

 

• Chilika Lake is renowned as a major wintering ground for migratory birds coming from as far as the Caspian Sea, Lake Baikal, and remote parts of Russia, Central and Southeast Asia.

 

• It is also home to the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin, and hosts Nalabana Bird Sanctuary, an island within the lagoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other important Ramsar wetland sites include Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan), Sundarbans Wetland (West Bengal), and Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir).

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1), Kerala (Option 2) and Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Chilika Lake is not located in any of these states; it lies specifically on the coast of Odisha.

question: Which of the following sites do “Not” have coal mines?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonipat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonipat, located in the state of Haryana, does not have coal mines; it is instead known as an industrial and agricultural hub in the National Capital Region. (सोनीपत — कोई कोयला खान नहीं)

 

• Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) is well known for its lignite (brown coal) deposits and is home to Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC India).

 

• Korba (Chhattisgarh) is one of India's major coalfields, often called the "Power Capital of Chhattisgarh" due to its coal mines and associated thermal power plants.

 

• Singareni (Telangana) is home to the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), a major coal mining company operating in the Godavari Valley coalfields.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major Indian coalfields include Jharia and Bokaro (Jharkhand), Raniganj (West Bengal), Talcher (Odisha), and Korba (Chhattisgarh).

 

NOTE

 

• Neyveli (Option 2): Has significant lignite mines/deposits in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Korba (Option 3): A major coal-mining and thermal power hub in Chhattisgarh.

 

• Singareni (Option 4): Site of the Singareni coal mines in Telangana, operated by SCCL.

question: Hema Malini, a well-known Bharatnatyam dancer and Bollywood actor, received which of the following honours of Indian civilians given by the Government of India in 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hema Malini, celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer and Bollywood actress, was conferred the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, by the Government of India in the year 2000. (हेमा मालिनी — पद्म श्री, वर्ष 2000)

 

• The Padma Shri is awarded for distinguished contribution in various fields, including art, literature, education, sports, medicine, social work and public affairs.

 

• She was later honoured with a higher award, the Padma Bhushan (India's third-highest civilian award), in 2012, for her contribution to Indian cinema and dance.

 

• Besides her acting career, Hema Malini has made notable contributions as a classical dancer, running her own dance institution, Natya Vihar Kalakendra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hema Malini has also served as a Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from Mathura, representing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day and are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in order of importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 1): India's highest civilian award; Hema Malini has not received this honour.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 3): Hema Malini received this award later, in 2012, not in 2000.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 4): India's second-highest civilian award; Hema Malini has not received this honour.

question: Which of the following dance forms is performed to Carnatic music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuchipudi, a classical dance form originating from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, is performed to Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India. (कुचिपुड़ी — कर्नाटक संगीत)

 

• Kuchipudi is a dance-drama form rooted in Hindu religious traditions, traditionally performed by all-male troupes as part of the Bhagavata Mela tradition, though today it is performed by both men and women, often as solo recitals.

 

• It uniquely combines fast rhythmic footwork with graceful movements, along with elements of speech (dialogue) within performance, distinguishing it from other classical dance forms.

 

• Carnatic music, characterised by its complex rhythmic structures (talas) and compositions (kritis), forms the musical backbone of South Indian classical dance forms such as Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu) is another major classical dance form performed to Carnatic music.

 

• Hindustani classical music forms the accompaniment for North Indian dance forms like Kathak.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A North Indian classical dance form performed to Hindustani classical music, not Carnatic.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): A classical dance from Odisha, performed to Odissi music, a distinct tradition with elements of both Hindustani and Carnatic styles, but not classified as Carnatic music itself.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): A classical dance from Assam, performed to Borgeet and Assamese devotional music, not Carnatic music.

question: If marginal propensity to consume is denoted by c, then government expenditure multiplier can be expressed as _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/1-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The government expenditure multiplier measures the change in national income (Y) resulting from a change in government spending (G), and is given by the formula k = 1/(1-c), where c is the marginal propensity to consume (MPC). (सरकारी व्यय गुणक — 1/(1-c))

 

• This formula arises from the simple Keynesian income-expenditure model, where an initial increase in government spending triggers successive rounds of consumption spending equal to c times the previous round's income increase, forming a geometric series that sums to 1/(1-c).

 

• Since 0 < c < 1 (MPC lies between 0 and 1), the multiplier 1/(1-c) is always greater than 1, meaning a given increase in government spending leads to an even larger increase in total national income.

 

• A higher MPC (people spending a larger share of additional income) results in a larger multiplier effect, since more of each round of income is re-spent rather than saved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The marginal propensity to save (MPS) is given by s = 1 - c; the government expenditure multiplier can also be written as 1/s.

 

• The tax multiplier, by contrast, is given by -c/(1-c), reflecting that changes in taxes have a smaller and opposite-signed effect on income compared to equivalent changes in government spending.

 

NOTE

 

• c (Option 1): This is simply the marginal propensity to consume itself, not the multiplier formula.

 

• 1/c (Option 3): An incorrect formula; it does not represent the government expenditure (income) multiplier.

 

• -1/c (Option 4): An incorrect, negatively signed formula; the government expenditure multiplier is always positive and equals 1/(1-c).
